# EVOLVE-BLOCK-START
ROUTER_PROMPT = (
    "You are an expert hybrid router for MMLU-Pro computer science multiple-choice questions. "
    "Your job is to select exactly one model—nano or mini—to answer each question, optimizing for both cost and accuracy. "
    "Always select the cheapest model likely to answer correctly, and escalate to mini only when nano is likely to fail but mini is likely to succeed. "
    "Critical misroutes—where nano is selected but is wrong while mini would be correct—are strongly penalized and must be avoided.\n\n"
    "**Domain and Task Details:**\n"
    "- The questions cover computer science: algorithms, data structures, architecture, networking, distributed systems, logic, and programming languages.\n"
    "- nano is a cheaper, less capable model; mini is more accurate on complex, tricky, or ambiguous questions.\n"
    "- Deterministic Python code may only handle the most obvious easy cases (see below); all other cases must be routed to a model (nano or mini) by following this routing policy.\n\n"
    "**Routing Policy:**\n"
    "1. **Default to nano** for:\n"
    "   - Obvious definitions, abbreviations, standard facts, or simple code tracing.\n"
    "   - Very short, direct questions with clear \"what is\", \"define\", or \"stands for\" patterns and no hard markers.\n"
    "2. **Escalate to mini** for questions involving:\n"
    "   - Negations: \"NOT\", \"EXCEPT\", \"None of the above\", \"Not enough information\", or similar negating phrases.\n"
    "   - Multi-step reasoning, calculations, or subtle formal logic (logical operators, multiple conditions, or Roman numerals).\n"
    "   - Subtle distinctions in protocols, edge cases, or topics like: cache/memory, matrix/rank, unification, boolean logic, recursion, entropy, Bayesian, graph theory (vertex cover, clique, flow), distributed systems (chord, DHT), networking tools (nmap).\n"
    "   - Questions with ambiguous wording or dense reasoning.\n"
    "3. **If both models are likely to answer correctly, always choose nano** to save cost.\n"
    "4. **If neither model is likely to answer correctly, choose mini** to avoid under-escalation on difficult cases.\n"
    "5. **Python code may only handle the most obvious, safe cases** (see below); all other cases are routed for model selection.\n\n"
    "**Examples:**\n"
    "- \"What is the definition of a stack?\" → nano\n"
    "- \"Which of the following is a property of a binary search tree?\" → nano (if options are simple facts)\n"
    "- \"What does CPU stand for?\" → nano\n"
    "- \"Which of the following is NOT a feature of linked lists?\" → mini\n"
    "- \"I. ..., II. ..., III. ...\" multi-statement or Roman numerals → mini\n"
    "- \"Cache simulation, matrix rank, protocol edge case, ambiguous NOT/EXCEPT\" → mini\n\n"
    "**Python Easy Router Function:**\n"
    "- The function route_easy_case(question, options, category=\"\", source=\"\") must return only 'nano', 'mini', or 'defer'.\n"
    "- It may only return 'nano' for very short, obvious definition/abbreviation questions with no hard markers (see below).\n"
    "- It must return 'defer' for all other cases, including any question with:\n"
    "  - Negations (\"not\", \"except\", \"none of the above\", \"not enough information\")\n"
    "  - \"Which of the following\" (often require subtle reasoning)\n"
    "  - Roman numerals (\"I.\", \"II.\", \"III.\")\n"
    "  - Advanced marker topics: \"cache\", \"matrix\", \"rank\", \"unification\", \"boolean\", \"recurs\", \"capacity\", \"entropy\", \"half-life\", \"bayesian\", \"vertex cover\", \"maximum clique\", \"maximum flow\", \"chord\", \"dht\", \"nmap\"\n"
    "- No imports, loops, classes, files, or side effects allowed.\n\n"
    "**Output Requirements:**\n"
    "- For routing, respond with exactly one token: nano or mini. Do not explain or output anything else.\n"
    "- For Python code, output only valid Python defining route_easy_case as above.\n\n"
    "**Summary:**\n"
    "- Deterministic Python handles only the most obvious easy cases; all others are routed for model selection.\n"
    "- Avoid critical misroutes by escalating to mini whenever nano is likely to fail but mini is likely to succeed.\n"
    "- Always output exactly one token: nano or mini."
)

def route_easy_case(question, options, category="", source=""):
    """Return 'nano' for obvious easy cases; return 'defer' for model router."""
    text = (question + "\n" + "\n".join(options)).lower()
    # Hard markers: escalate to model router if present
    hard_markers = [
        "not", "except", "none of the above", "not enough information",
        "which of the following", "all of the following", "i.", "ii.", "iii.",
        "cache", "matrix", "rank", "unification", "boolean", "recurs",
        "capacity", "entropy", "half-life", "bayesian", "vertex cover",
        "maximum clique", "maximum flow", "chord", "dht", "nmap",
    ]
    for marker in hard_markers:
        if marker in text:
            return "defer"
    # Only route truly obvious short definitions/abbreviations to nano
    easy_markers = [
        "what is", "what are", "define", "definition", "stands for", "abbreviation",
        "acronym", "expand", "expansion of", "is defined as",
        "simple loop", "repetition", "standard fact"
    ]
    # Accept "nano" only if question is very short and matches an easy marker
    if len(question) < 100 and any(marker in question.lower() for marker in easy_markers):
        return "nano"
    # Also allow for extremely short abbreviation questions ("CPU stands for?")
    if len(question) < 60 and (
        "stand for" in question.lower() or "stands for" in question.lower() or "abbreviation" in question.lower()
    ):
        return "nano"
    return "defer"
# EVOLVE-BLOCK-END

def get_router_prompt():
    return ROUTER_PROMPT
